item.title: Nearly 90,000 told to evacuate as wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada
item.description:
‘Human-caused’, wind-driven fire in Reno leaves thousands of homes and businesses without power, officials say Authorities have ordered the evacuation of about 90,000 residents of Reno, Nevada , and the adjacent North Valley as a fast-moving, wind-driven wildfire bears down on the city. The Hawk fire began on Saturday to the north-west of the city, and quickly grew, showing “extreme fire behavior” as it threatened foothill neighborhoods in Nevada’s second-largest city. It stood at a little more than 15,000 acres burned on Monday morning, and was 0% contained. Continue reading...

item.title: UK PM Burnham vows support for Ukraine despite 'outrageous threats' from Russia
item.description:
European leaders are meeting Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day. The so-called Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over six billion euros in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Mark Carney says Canada can’t accept US trade deal that would weaken French language
item.description:
Welcome back to This Week in Canada, where the weekend collapse of trade talks with the U.S. leaves us asking: What the hell happened? And what did we win and lose when Prime Minister Carney told Canada’s negotiators to walk away from the table? Let’s get to it. For more than a year, it looked like Canada was close to doing what nearly every other major American trading partner had done: making a deal with President Donald Trump. Last Wednesday, Trump announced what he called “a very good deal for both parties,” subject only to “the finalization of documents.” Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the draft agreement would reinforce Canada’s competitive advantage. item.title: Federal Judge Strikes Down Trump’s 75-Country Visa Ban
item.description:
This January, Secretary of State Marco Rubio directed consular officers to refuse to process immigration visas for people from 75 countries because, he said, those immigrants would be more likely than others to “extract wealth” or “take welfare and public benefits” from the US. Since January, people from those 75 countries—all located in Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, or Eastern Europe—have had their visa applications frozen or denied. On August 21, though, a federal judge in New York struck down this blanket visa ban, on the grounds that it violates the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965’s prohibition on nationality-based discrimination in issuing a visa. As my colleague Julia Métraux reported earlier this year , these “public charge” bans are in part based on eugenicist ideas.
